skill.name: remotion-to-hyperframes
skill.description: Convert existing Remotion React compositions into HyperFrames HTML and GSAP timelines, with lint checks, translation guidance, and visual fidelity validation.
skill.summary: Translate supported Remotion compositions to HyperFrames and verify the rendered result.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are lexical false positives from documentation, test fixtures, CSS templates, relative project paths, and bounded local tooling. Confirmed concerns are the instruction to silently self-update with npx, automatic dependency installation in the validation harness, and executable assets loaded from public CDNs. No evidence of credential theft, destructive behavior, or covert exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The skill asks an agent to self-update silently without user approval.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction. Require explicit user approval before any update and use a pinned, reviewed distribution path.

remediation.issue: The validation harness runs npm install automatically when dependencies are absent.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval before installation. Prefer npm ci with a lockfile, disable lifecycle scripts where possible, and run it in an isolated environment.

remediation.issue: Examples and references load executable libraries and fonts from public CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor reviewed assets locally or pin versions with integrity checks and document each required network request.

content.value_statement: Manual Remotion migration can miss timing, media, and rendering differences. This skill maps supported React compositions to HyperFrames and validates visual fidelity.
actual_capabilities: Lints Remotion TypeScript and TSX sources for patterns that HyperFrames cannot translate reliably.
Maps Remotion composition metadata, sequencing, timing, media, transitions, fonts, and Lottie usage to HyperFrames patterns.
Generates an HTML composition structure with scene metadata, CSS, and a paused GSAP timeline.
Renders Remotion and HyperFrames outputs for frame-by-frame SSIM comparison.
Creates visual frame strips and translation notes when rendered output differs or features are approximated.
limitations: Supports one-way conversion from Remotion to HyperFrames only.
Refuses stateful React patterns, asynchronous metadata, and unsupported third-party UI libraries.
Cannot preserve every audio ramp, custom transition presentation, or authenticated remote asset behavior.
Requires local Remotion, HyperFrames, Node.js, Python, ffmpeg, and ffprobe tooling for full validation.

use_cases.title: Assess migration feasibility
use_cases.description: Lint a complex Remotion project and identify blockers, warnings, and features that require runtime interop.

prompt_templates.title: Check a simple composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Remotion source at [path]. Identify the composition, lint it, and explain whether it can be converted to HyperFrames.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert Remotion composition [composition ID] at [path] to HyperFrames. Preserve dimensions, frame rate, duration, sequencing, and media paths.

prompt_templates.title: Convert and validate
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert [composition ID] from Remotion to HyperFrames. Render both versions, compare SSIM, inspect failed frames, and document every approximation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a complex migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Remotion project at [path]. Classify blockers and warnings, select one composition, propose interop where needed, and produce a validated migration plan.

output_examples.input: Check whether a title card using Sequence, interpolate, spring, and staticFile can migrate.
output_examples.output: The composition is eligible. The report lists direct HyperFrames mappings, copied assets, expected metadata, and the validation steps.

output_examples.input: Convert a composition that uses useState and a frame-dependent useEffect.
output_examples.output: The conversion stops after linting. The report identifies stateful behavior and recommends runtime interop instead of lossy HTML translation.
The result includes Remotion and HyperFrames renders, SSIM statistics, a pass decision, divergent frame samples, and documented limitations.

best_practices: Run the source linter before generating any HyperFrames files.
Translate one composition at a time and preserve its original frame rate, dimensions, and duration.
Use matching pixel formats and review both SSIM metrics and frame strips.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create a new composition from a visual reference.
Do not force conversion when the linter reports stateful React or asynchronous metadata blockers.
Do not treat a visual similarity score as proof that audio and remote assets are equivalent.

faq.question: Can this skill convert HyperFrames back to Remotion?
faq.answer: No. The supported direction is Remotion to HyperFrames only.

faq.question: Does it support every React component?
faq.answer: No. Stateful hooks, asynchronous metadata, and several third-party UI libraries require refactoring or runtime interop.

faq.question: How does it verify visual accuracy?
faq.answer: It renders both compositions and computes frame-level SSIM statistics. A frame strip helps diagnose visible differences.

faq.question: What happens to unsupported features?
faq.answer: Blockers stop conversion. Lower-impact gaps are approximated or removed and recorded in translation notes.

faq.question: Can it migrate multiple compositions together?
faq.answer: No. Select and convert one Remotion composition at a time.

faq.question: Which tools are required for full validation?
faq.answer: Full validation requires Node.js, Remotion, HyperFrames, Python, ffmpeg, and ffprobe in the local environment.
